root_cause.text: The IDLETIMER target allows reuse of timer labels across different revisions without checking whether the existing timer uses alarm timer semantics (revision 1) or a regular timer_list (revision 0), causing revision 0 rules to call mod_timer() on an uninitialized timer->timer when the label was created with XT_IDLETIMER_ALARM.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "If the label was created first by revision 1 with XT_IDLETIMER_ALARM, the object uses alarm timer semantics and timer->timer is never initialized. Reusing that object from revision 0 causes mod_timer() on an uninitialized timer_list." The fix adds a rejection check: `if (info->timer->timer_type & XT_IDLETIMER_ALARM)` before allowing reuse.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard against creating an idletimer rule with a label that already belongs to an ALARM timer, ensuring consistent timer type per label.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check that rejects the addition of a new idletimer rule if an existing timer with the same label has the XT_IDLETIMER_ALARM flag set, returning -EINVAL.
intent_record.how: When attempting to add a new rule with a label that already exists, the code now verifies whether the existing timer is of type ALARM. If so, the operation is aborted with an error, preventing two rules with the same label but different timer types from coexisting.

candidates.rationale: The mod_timer call is made unconditionally when the label already exists, without checking whether the existing timer uses alarm timer semantics (revision 1) or a regular timer_list (revision 0). If the label was created with XT_IDLETIMER_ALARM, the timer member is uninitialized or of a different type, leading to undefined behavior.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement modifies an existing timer without verifying whether the timer is a regular timer_list (revision 0) or an alarm timer (revision 1). If the label was created with XT_IDLETIMER_ALARM, the timer member is uninitialized or incompatible, causing undefined behavior when mod_timer is called.
